EU-backed SPARK project begins in Skagen

19 May 2026

An international consortium led by Stillstrom by Maersk has secured EUR 5 million from Horizon Europe to develop and demonstrate offshore charging infrastructure for vessels at anchor.

SPARK brings together eight partners from five countries for a 36-month project centred on an Offshore Power Zone outside Skagen, Denmark. The pilot will enable a stationary vessel to connect to an at-sea power point supplied through the nearby Port of Skagen.

The first live demonstration will support one ship connection. It will test how the technology performs in an operational environment while the consortium examines vessel integration, port infrastructure, safety, simulation, commercial viability and regulatory pathways.

By replacing electricity generated by auxiliary engines, the project aims to reduce emissions, local air pollution and noise from vessels waiting between operations. The knowledge developed in Skagen will help prepare the solution for replication and expansion in other anchorage locations.
